S58.01.needs: Signed in, with the AGI CLI available. At least one MCP server configured helps; none shows the empty message.
S58.01.note: The header button has tooltip "More" in the code, so the tester sees that word, not "More actions". The list also appears in Settings under "MCP servers".
steps: Sign in, then open the AGI chat panel in the editor.
Click the "..." button in the panel header (tooltip "More").
Click "MCP servers" in the menu.

Look at the list titled "Code, MCP servers". Each configured server is a row with its name, status, transport and scope. With none configured it shows "No MCP servers are configured yet" and "Add an MCP server". Compare with Expected.
S58.01.where: Chat panel > More (the "..." button in the panel header) > MCP servers. Or Command Palette > Code: Show MCP Servers

S58.07.needs: A configured MCP server. A user-added server is needed for the row to offer actions when its status is not blocked or off.
S58.07.note: The "Test connection" action appears only when the server is not blocked or off. Success text comes from the "mcp.connected" message in apps/extension-vscode/packages/ui path (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json) and reads "Code: {name} connected in {ms} ms and offers {count} tools.".
steps: Open the chat panel and click the "..." button in its header.
Click "MCP servers", then click a server row (not a Remove action).
In the "Choose an action" list, click "Test connection".
Watch for a notification such as "connected in N ms and offers N tools" (success), or a failure message saying the server "did not connect" with a reason. Compare with Expected.
S58.07.where: Chat panel > More > MCP servers > click a server row > Test connection

S58.08.needs: A configured MCP server that connects, so its tools can be listed.
S58.08.note: The code lists tools only when the person chooses "Show tools"; adding a server does not show its tools automatically, which differs from the wording of Expected.
steps: Open the chat panel, click the "..." button in its header, then click "MCP servers".
Click a server row. In the "Choose an action" list, click "Show tools".
Look at the list titled with the server name. Under the "Tools" heading, each tool is shown with its name and description.
If the server has no tools, the list says "This server offers no tools". Compare with Expected.
S58.08.where: Chat panel > More > MCP servers > click a server row > Show tools

S58.11.needs: A configured MCP server that is not blocked or off, so the details action appears.
S58.11.note: The details show the server's advertised capabilities as a list, not a fixed list of tools, resources, prompts and extensions. Whether those names appear depends on what the server reports.
steps: Open the chat panel, click the "..." button in its header, then click "MCP servers".
Click a server row, then click "Server details" (or use the info button on the row).
A text document named "<server name> MCP server" opens. Read its "Protocol", "Server" and "Capabilities" lines.
Compare the fields shown with Expected (protocol, tools, resources, prompts, extensions).
S58.11.where: Chat panel > More > MCP servers > click a server row > Server details

S58.12.needs: A configured MCP server that is not blocked or off.
S58.12.note: The code shows recent server output only. It has no call history, so the "call history" part of Expected is not in the code.
steps: Open the chat panel, click the "..." button in its header, then click "MCP servers".
Click a server row, then click "Server details".
Read the "Health" line in the document: "Responding", "Connected, but it did not answer a ping" or "Did not connect".
Scroll to the "Recent output" section. It shows server logs, or "No output from this server yet." Compare with Expected.
S58.12.where: Chat panel > More > MCP servers > click a server row > Server details

S58.14.needs: A workspace with a project-scoped MCP server already configured outside the extension, since the extension cannot create one.
S58.14.note: The extension's "Add an MCP server" flow saves only user-scoped servers, with no project choice, so per-project configuration is not set from the UI; project servers are only shown as "From this workspace". Searched apps/extension-vscode for a project-scope setting or add option and found none.
steps: Open the MCP servers list from the chat panel's "..." menu, or run Code: Show MCP Servers.
Look for a server whose row description ends with "project" or whose Settings row says "From this workspace".
Compare with Expected: that server should load only in this project.
S58.14.where: Code: Show MCP Servers (Chat panel > More > MCP servers), then read the row description ending in "project"; Settings > MCP servers shows "From this workspace"
